questions.question: Marks in statistics of 12 students are x, 28, 35, 56, 78, 63, 65, 81, 79, 83, 80, y, where x and y are the lowest and highest marks, respectively. If the range and average of the marks are 70 and 64, respectively, then the ordered pair (x, y) is:
questions.solution: __Shortcut Trick__ Sum of **lowest (x)** and **highest (y)** marks = (Average × Total students) − Sum of other 10 marks. x + y = (64 × 12) − 648 = 768 − 648 = 120. Given **Range** (y − x) = 70. Solving: y = (120 + 70) ÷ 2 = 95 and x = (120 − 70) ÷ 2 = 25. **∴ The correct answer is (25 , 95).** **__Alternate Method__** **Given:** Marks of **12 students**, Average = 64, Range = 70, x = lowest, y = highest. **Formula Used:** Average = Sum ÷ Count | Range = Highest − Lowest [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/135b31fb26238b35f1cc2c3a928fd68538b3fe7fb7d3c71342a98f38f0165e0d.png] ⇒ Sum of all 12 marks = 12 × 64 = 768 ⇒ Sum of known 10 marks = 28 + 35 + 56 + 78 + 63 + 65 + 81 + 79 + 83 + 80 = 648 ⇒ x + y = 768 − 648 = 120 ⇒ y − x = 70 (Given Range) ⇒ Adding both: 2y = 190 ⇒ y = 95 ⇒ Subtracting: 2x = 50 ⇒ x = 25 **∴ The correct answer is (25 , 95).** **__Additional Information__** Range in Statistics

questions.question: The mode and median of a dataset is 52.7 and 65, respectively. What is the mean of the dataset? (Use empirical formula, and round off your answer to one decimal place.)
questions.solution: __Shortcut Trick__ Apply the **Empirical Formula**: **Mean = (3 × Median − Mode) ÷ 2**. Substitute the given values: **Mean = (3 × 65 − 52.7) ÷ 2**. **Mean = (195 − 52.7) ÷ 2 = 142.3 ÷ 2 = 71.15**. Rounding to one decimal place, we get **71.2**. **∴ The correct answer is 71.2.** **__Alternate Method__** **Given:** **Mode** = 52.7 and **Median** = 65. **Formula Used:** **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9c6435b5decb3f386276b8f9c1ecee96cb4dc2f9570c85aab79fab57c15c3399.png] ⇒ 52.7 = 3 × 65 − 2 × Mean ⇒ 52.7 = 195 − 2 × Mean ⇒ 2 × Mean = 195 − 52.7 ⇒ 2 × Mean = 142.3 ⇒ Mean = 142.3 ÷ 2 ⇒ Mean = 71.15 ≈ 71.2 **∴ The correct answer is 71.2.** **__Additional Information__** Empirical Relationship The relationship **Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean** is an approximation used for **unimodal** and **moderately skewed** distributions.

questions.question: The arithmetic mean of the observations 28, 31, 40, 63, 57, 37, 34, 70 and 99 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume an **assumed mean** of 50.

Calculate **deviations** from 50: −22, −19, −10, +13, +7, −13, −16, +20, +49.

Net deviation = (−22 − 19 − 10 − 13 − 16) + (13 + 7 + 20 + 49) = −80 + 89 = +9.

Average deviation = 9 ÷ 9 = +1.

Actual Mean = Assumed Mean + Average Deviation = 50 + 1 = 51.

**∴ The correct answer is 51.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Observations are 28, 31, 40, 63, 57, 37, 34, 70, and 99.

**Formula Used:** Arithmetic Mean = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a911a5d8c44ed39bfa1927880f845c3381b551c7250b6f73d7baf3b89e34112.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total number of observations (n) = 9

⇒ Sum of observations = 28 + 31 + 40 + 63 + 57 + 37 + 34 + 70 + 99

⇒ Sum = 459

⇒ Arithmetic Mean = 459 ÷ 9

⇒ Arithmetic Mean = 51

**∴ The correct answer is 51.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Arithmetic Mean

The sum of **deviations** of a set of observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero. If each observation is increased by a constant 'k', the mean also increases by 'k'.

Median

The **Median** is the middle value when observations are arranged in ascending order. For n = 9, it is the (9+1)÷2 = 5th term.

Relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode

For a moderately skewed distribution: **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**.</p

For a perfectly **symmetrical distribution**, Mean = Median = Mode.

questions.question: The mode and median of data are 36.3 and 62, respectively. What is the mean of the data? (Use the empirical formula)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **Empirical Formula**: **Mean = (3 × Median − Mode) ÷ 2**.

Mean = (3 × 62 − 36.3) ÷ 2

Mean = (186 − 36.3) ÷ 2

Mean = 149.7 ÷ 2 = 74.85

**∴ The correct answer is 74.85.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Mode** = 36.3 and **Median** = 62.

**Formula Used:** **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a082657453041fee45692e7447d27f07bd490e4078ae48fa46db0e2c00adb6e8.png] 

⇒ 36.3 = 3 × 62 − 2 × Mean

⇒ 36.3 = 186 − 2 × Mean

⇒ 2 × Mean = 186 − 36.3

⇒ 2 × Mean = 149.7

⇒ Mean = 149.7 ÷ 2

⇒ Mean = 74.85

**∴ The correct answer is 74.85.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship

For a **moderately skewed distribution**, the relationship between central tendencies is **Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean**.

Symmetrical Distribution

In a perfectly **symmetrical distribution** (like a Normal Distribution), the **Mean, Median, and Mode** coincide at the same point (Mean = Median = Mode).

Skewness and Central Tendency

In a **positively skewed** distribution, **Mean > Median > Mode**. In a **negatively skewed** distribution, **Mode > Median > Mean**.</p

questions.question: Following are the ages (in years) of 6 people in a group: 25, 30, 35, 40, 45 and 50. What is the standard deviation of their ages (rounded to two decimal places)?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The given ages form an **Arithmetic Progression (AP)** with common difference **d = 5** and number of terms **n = 6**.

Shortcut formula for **Standard Deviation (σ)** of an AP: σ = d × √[(n² − 1) / 12]

σ = 5 × √[(6² − 1) / 12] = 5 × √(35 / 12) = 5 × √2.9167

σ ≈ 5 × 1.7078 = 8.539

**∴ The correct answer is 8.54 years.**

Mean = (3 × 60 − 14.2) ÷ 2 Mean = (180 − 14.2) ÷ 2 Mean = 165.8 ÷ 2 = 82.9 **∴ The correct answer is 82.9.** **__Alternate Method__** **Given:** **Mode** of the data set = 14.2 **Median** of the data set = 60 **Formula Used:** The **Empirical Formula** for a moderately skewed distribution is: **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/504fc5715517174c6adab68e6fe2b4aa8a3eb99aa62930e696eb7701f5e816c7.png] **Calculations:** ⇒ 14.2 = 3 × 60 − 2 × Mean ⇒ 14.2 = 180 − 2 × Mean ⇒ 2 × Mean = 180 − 14.2 ⇒ 2 × Mean = 165.8 ⇒ Mean = 165.8 ÷ 2 ⇒ Mean = 82.9 **∴ The correct answer is 82.9.** **__Additional Information__** Empirical Relationship The **empirical relationship** between Mean, Median, and Mode is used for **unimodal** and **moderately skewed** distributions.

questions.question: The median of the observations 87, 56, 79, 81, 11, 53, 94, 45, 32, 99 and 98 is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Arrange the given **11 observations** in **ascending order**:

11, 32, 45, 53, 56, **79**, 81, 87, 94, 98, 99

Since the number of terms (N = 11) is **odd**, the **median** is the exact middle term:

Median = ((11 + 1) ÷ 2)th term = 6th term = **79**

**∴ The correct answer is 79.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Observations: 87, 56, 79, 81, 11, 53, 94, 45, 32, 99, 98

Total number of observations (N) = 11

**Formula Used:**

When N is odd, Median = ((N + 1) ÷ 2)th term (after arranging in ascending order).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9efd99bf419560cc57b33a65083d202083d4ae287cd8a464483057ab995f4c93.png] 

**Calculations:**

First, arrange the given observations in ascending order:

⇒ 11, 32, 45, 53, 56, 79, 81, 87, 94, 98, 99

Count the total number of observations:

⇒ N = 11

Since N is an odd number, the median is calculated as:

⇒ Median = ((N + 1) ÷ 2)th term

⇒ Median = ((11 + 1) ÷ 2)th term

⇒ Median = (12 ÷ 2)th term

⇒ Median = 6th term

Looking at the ordered list, the 6th term is 79.

⇒ Median = 79

**Option Analysis:**

⇒ **Option (1) 53:** This is the 4th term in the sorted list, not the middle term.

⇒ **Option (2) 56:** This is the 5th term in the sorted list, which is just before the middle term.

⇒ **Option (3) 81:** This is the 7th term in the sorted list, which is just after the middle term.

⇒ **Option (4) 79:** This is the exact 6th (middle) term, which is the correct median.

**∴ The correct answer is 79.**

**__Additional Information__**

Median for Even Number of Terms

If the number of observations (N) is even, the median is the average of the (N ÷ 2)th term and the ((N ÷ 2) + 1)th term after arranging them in ascending order.

Relation between Mean, Median, and Mode

For a moderately skewed distribution, the empirical relationship is: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Effect of Outliers on Median

Unlike the mean, the median is a robust measure of central tendency and is not heavily influenced by extremely large or small values (outliers).</p

questions.question:
What is the mean of the following distribution?

 
 

 Marks
 13 
 27 
 59 
 61 
 97 
 
 
 
 

 No. of Students
 95 
 57 
 80 
 98 
 73
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Total Frequency** (Σf) = 95 + 57 + 80 + 98 + 73 = 403

**Sum of Products** (Σfx) = (13 × 95) + (27 × 57) + (59 × 80) + (61 × 98) + (97 × 73)

Σfx = 1235 + 1539 + 4720 + 5978 + 7081 = 20553

**Mean** = Σfx / Σf = 20553 / 403 = 51

**∴ The correct answer is 51.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Marks** (x) and **Number of Students** (f).

**Formula:** **Mean** (μ) = Σ(fᵢ × xᵢ) / Σfᵢ

⇒ **Total Students** (Σf) = 95 + 57 + 80 + 98 + 73 = 403

⇒ f₁x₁ = 13 × 95 = 1235

⇒ f₂x₂ = 27 × 57 = 1539

⇒ f₃x₃ = 59 × 80 = 4720

⇒ f₄x₄ = 61 × 98 = 5978

⇒ f₅x₅ = 97 × 73 = 7081

⇒ **Sum of Products** (Σfx) = 1235 + 1539 + 4720 + 5978 + 7081 = 20553

⇒ **Mean** = 20553 / 403 = 51

**∴ The correct answer is 51.**

**__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean

The **average** of a set of numerical values, calculated by dividing the **sum of the values** by the **total count** of observations.

Assumed Mean Method

A technique to simplify calculations by choosing an **arbitrary value** 'A' and using **deviations** d = x − A. Formula: Mean = A + (Σfd / Σf).

Weighted Mean

Used when different values have different **levels of importance** (weights), calculated as Σ(w × x) / Σw.</p

questions.question: The mean and the mode of a data set are 33.9 and 40.1, respectively. Find the median of the data, using the empirical formula. (Round off your answer to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **Empirical Formula**: 3 × **Median** = **Mode** + 2 × **Mean**.

3 × **Median** = 40.1 + 2 × 33.9

3 × **Median** = 40.1 + 67.8 = 107.9

**Median** = 107.9 ÷ 3 = 35.966...

Rounding to two decimal places, we get 35.97.

**∴ The correct answer is 35.97.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Mean** = 33.9

**Mode** = 40.1

**Formula Used:**

**Mode** = 3(**Median**) − 2(**Mean**)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/72182fbfe79f7b38561ac77b7e670c541cbe31f7e6f8d204215b9291b59f286b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 40.1 = 3 × **Median** − 2 × 33.9

⇒ 40.1 = 3 × **Median** − 67.8

⇒ 3 × **Median** = 40.1 + 67.8

⇒ 3 × **Median** = 107.9

⇒ **Median** = 107.9 ÷ 3

⇒ **Median** = 35.9666...

⇒ **Median** ≈ 35.97

**∴ The correct answer is 35.97.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship is **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**.

Symmetric Distribution

In a perfectly **Symmetric Distribution**, the values of **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** are all equal (Mean = Median = Mode).

Skewness Identification

If **Mode > Median > Mean**, the distribution is **Negatively Skewed** (skewed to the left). If **Mean > Median > Mode**, it is **Positively Skewed**.</p

questions.question: The mean and the mode of a data set are 51.5 and 61.7, respectively. Find the median of the data set, using the empirical formula.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **Empirical Formula**: **3 × Median = Mode + 2 × Mean**.

3 × Median = 61.7 + 2 × 51.5

3 × Median = 61.7 + 103 = 164.7

Median = 164.7 ÷ 3 = 54.9

**∴ The correct answer is 54.9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Mean** = 51.5, **Mode** = 61.7

**Formula Used:** **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c43dd7a92943be8bd4363b53e8b8ed4ad7088dd48727cde72641a27b5229c3c1.png] 

⇒ 61.7 = 3 × Median − 2 × 51.5

⇒ 61.7 = 3 × Median − 103

⇒ 3 × Median = 61.7 + 103

⇒ 3 × Median = 164.7

⇒ Median = 164.7 ÷ 3

⇒ Median = 54.9

**∴ The correct answer is 54.9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship

For a **moderately skewed distribution**, the relationship between central tendencies is **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**.

Symmetric Distribution

In a perfectly **symmetrical distribution** (like a Normal Distribution), the **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** are all identical.

Skewness and Central Tendency

In **positively skewed** data, Mean > Median > Mode. In **negatively skewed** data, Mode > Median > Mean.</p

questions.question: The median of the observations 71, 95, 67, 55, 78, 45, 58, 44, 69, 41 and 88 is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Arrange the given **11 observations** in ascending order:

41, 44, 45, 55, 58, **67**, 69, 71, 78, 88, 95

Since the number of terms (N = 11) is **odd**, the median is the middle term:

Median = ((N + 1) ÷ 2)th term = 6th term = **67**

**∴ The correct answer is 67.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given observations:** 71, 95, 67, 55, 78, 45, 58, 44, 69, 41, 88

**Total number of observations (N):** 11

**Formula:**

When N is odd, Median = Value of ((N + 1) ÷ 2)th observation in the sorted list.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f36c64e4a7dafe355fca23dec005cacb9cba1d165aee20c84873eac12bb863e0.png] 

Step-by-step calculation:

⇒ Arrange the data in ascending order: 41, 44, 45, 55, 58, 67, 69, 71, 78, 88, 95

⇒ Count of observations (N) = 11

⇒ Since N is odd, Median = ((11 + 1) ÷ 2)th term

⇒ Median = 6th term

⇒ 6th term in the sorted list is 67.

⇒ Therefore, the median of the given observations is 67.

**Why other options are incorrect:**

⇒ **Option (1) 69:** This is the 7th term in the sorted list, not the middle term.

⇒ **Option (3) 55:** This is the 4th term in the sorted list, which is not the middle term.

⇒ **Option (4) 58:** This is the 5th term in the sorted list, which is not the middle term.

**∴ The correct answer is 67.**

**__Additional Information__**

Median for Even Number of Terms

If N is even, the median is the average of the (N ÷ 2)th and ((N ÷ 2) + 1)th terms. Formula: Median = [Value of (N/2)th term + Value of (N/2 + 1)th term] ÷ 2.

Mean (Arithmetic Average)

The sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations. Formula: Mean = (Sum of all observations) ÷ N.

Mode

The value that appears most frequently in a data set. A data set can have one mode, more than one mode, or no mode at all.

Empirical Relationship

The relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode for moderately skewed distributions. Formula: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.</p

questions.question:
What is the mode of the following data?

41, 55, 45, 48, 40, 47, 41, 47, 54, 44, 49, 48, 53, 54, 50, 53, 41, 46
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Mode** is the value that appears most frequently in a dataset.

By observing the given dataset, we count the frequency of each number:

The number **41** appears **3 times**, which is the highest frequency among all numbers.

All other numbers appear 2 times or fewer.

**∴ The correct answer is 41.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The dataset is: 41, 55, 45, 48, 40, 47, 41, 47, 54, 44, 49, 48, 53, 54, 50, 53, 41, 46

**Formula Used:**

Mode = Value with the maximum frequency in the dataset.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/db5f1454a3e8d96abbfd4d72cf0897f64e0beb5d90300b5ab1b712b58d3fa5d3.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let us arrange the data in ascending order to count the frequencies systematically:

40, 41, 41, 41, 44, 45, 46, 47, 47, 48, 48, 49, 50, 53, 53, 54, 54, 55

Now, let us list the frequency of each observation:

⇒ Frequency of 40 = 1

⇒ Frequency of **41** = **3**

⇒ Frequency of 44 = 1

⇒ Frequency of 45 = 1

⇒ Frequency of 46 = 1

⇒ Frequency of 47 = 2

⇒ Frequency of 48 = 2

⇒ Frequency of 49 = 1

⇒ Frequency of 50 = 1

⇒ Frequency of 53 = 2

⇒ Frequency of 54 = 2

⇒ Frequency of 55 = 1

Since the number **41** has the maximum frequency of 3, the mode of the given data is 41.

Let us analyze why the other options are incorrect:

⇒ Option (1) 45: Frequency is 1, which is not the maximum.

⇒ Option (2) 55: Frequency is 1, which is not the maximum.

⇒ Option (3) 48: Frequency is 2, which is less than 3.

⇒ Option (4) 41: Frequency is 3, which is the maximum.

**∴ The correct answer is 41.**

**__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship is given by: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Types of Mode Distributions

A dataset can have one mode (unimodal), two modes (bimodal), three modes (trimodal), or no mode if all values occur with the same frequency.

Median of a Dataset

The middle value when the data is arranged in ascending or descending order. For N terms, if N is odd, Median = ((N+1)/2)th term; if N is even, Median = Average of (N/2)th and (N/2 + 1)th terms.</p

questions.question: If the mode of a data exceeds its mean by 12.6, then the mode exceeds the median by _____. (Use empirical formula.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Empirical Formula** can be rewritten as: (**Mode** − **Mean**) = 3 × (**Median** − **Mean**).

Given: **Mode** − **Mean** = 12.6.

⇒ 12.6 = 3 × (**Median** − **Mean**) ⇒ (**Median** − **Mean**) = 4.2.

We need (**Mode** − **Median**) = (**Mode** − **Mean**) − (**Median** − **Mean**).

⇒ (**Mode** − **Median**) = 12.6 − 4.2 = 8.4.

<p

questions.question: If the mode of a data set exceeds its mean by 17.7, then the mode exceeds the median by _____. (Use empirical formula.)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Using the direct relation derived from the **empirical formula**:

(**Mode** − **Median**) = 2/3 × (**Mode** − **Mean**)

Given: (**Mode** − **Mean**) = **17.7**

∴ (**Mode** − **Median**) = 2/3 × 17.7 = 2 × 5.9 = **11.8**

**∴ The correct answer is 11.8.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Mode** − **Mean** = **17.7**

**Formula Used:** **Mode** = 3 × **Median** − 2 × **Mean**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b2624f18997784bb1414b2d7b4f6be8c98c52b6e478098d7881c7b4c4f1e488c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Mode** = 3 × **Median** − 2 × **Mean**

⇒ **Mode** + 2 × **Mean** = 3 × **Median**

⇒ From given, **Mean** = **Mode** − 17.7

⇒ **Mode** = 3 × **Median** − 2 × (**Mode** − 17.7)

⇒ **Mode** = 3 × **Median** − 2 × **Mode** + 35.4

⇒ 3 × **Mode** − 3 × **Median** = 35.4

⇒ 3 × (**Mode** − **Median**) = 35.4

⇒ **Mode** − **Median** = 35.4 ÷ 3

⇒ **Mode** − **Median** = **11.8**

**∴ The correct answer is 11.8.**

**__Additional Information__**

Empirical Formula

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship is **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**.

Symmetrical Distribution

In a perfectly **symmetrical distribution**, the **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** are all equal (**Mean = Median = Mode**).

Skewness Relation

The difference (**Mean** − **Mode**) is approximately three times the difference (**Mean** − **Median**).</p

Since the number of terms (n = 11) is **odd**, the **median** is the middle-most term:

Median = ((11 + 1) ÷ 2)th term = **6th term** = **53**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Observations: 93, 38, 12, 55, 70, 98, 60, 49, 53, 11, 38

When the number of observations (n) is **odd**:

Count the number of observations:

⇒ n = 11 (which is an **odd number**)

Apply the median formula for odd n:

⇒ Median = ((11 + 1) ÷ 2)th term

⇒ Median = (12 ÷ 2)th term

⇒ Median = **6th term**

Looking at the sorted list, the 6th term is **53**.

Mean, Median, and Mode Relationship

For a moderately skewed distribution, the empirical relationship is: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Properties of Median

The median is not affected by extremely large or small values (outliers), making it a better measure of central tendency than the mean for skewed data.</p

questions.question: The mean and standard deviation of 100 terms are 50 and 3, respectively. The sum of squares of the 100 terms is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct relation: **Sum of Squares** = **n** × (**Variance** + **Mean**²).

Given **n** = 100, **Mean** = 50, and **Standard Deviation** = 3.

**Variance** = 3² = 9.

**Sum of Squares** = 100 × (9 + 50²) = 100 × (9 + 2500) = 2,50,900.

**∴ The correct answer is 2,50,900.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**
